newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks forge to higher close on BHP.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks forge to higher close on BHP.

text.p: Investor enthusiasm over The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd's plan to revamp its steel division helped drive Australian shares to their highest close in over two months on Tuesday.
Brokers said BHP's plan to shut down steel production at its Newcastle plant, BHP's oldest, by 1999 was well-received and had buoyed the market overall.
"That has been the major impetus for the market as a whole," said John Paterson, managing director at J.B. Were Stockbroking.
The key All Ordinaries Index closed up 17.4 points at 2,479.1, its highest close since February 27.
A strong futures market also underpinned the market. The June share price index closed up 26 points at 2,486, a seven point premium to the physical market.

But it was BHP's announcement soon after the market's open that fired the market higher. It said it planned to lay off 2,500 workers at Newcastle and shut down other smaller steel processing plants to save more than A$500 million ($390 million).

BHP closed up 48 cents or 2.79 percent at A$17.86, and some brokers predicted Australia's largest listed company would rumble up to A$18 as analysts assessed the extent of the expected recovery of BHP's ailing steel division.
Brokers said BHP's boost to the resources sector was matched by continued strength in the banking sector, led by a buoyant NAB, and a media sector basking in good news from the United States.
Ord Minnett Institutional Director Eric Gale pointed to the strength in the media sector and the Seven Network Ltd in particular.

MGM, which is owned by a joint venture of Seven and U.S. billionaire Kirk Kerkorian, announced on Monday it would buy Metromedia's studio and film library assets for US$573 million to give MGM the largest modern film library in the world.

Seven said later it would buy just US$39 million of MGM stock to fund the deal, while Kerkorian's Tracinda Corp would subscribe to buy US$321 million of MGM stock. Seven said however it would continue to have a 50 percent voting share in MGM.
"That certainly looks a good deal," said Ord Minnett's Gale.
Seven's shares rose 19 cents or 4.1 percent to A$4.80 on over 1.8 million shares traded.
